brief: The canvas presents a dynamic field of interconnected, fluid geometric forms. The forms continuously drift and interact, undergoing cycles between states of deep, subtle equilibrium and moments of high mechanical stress. Viewing is a constant experience of transformation, where structures shift and reform. The color shifts are either slow and near-monochromatic, suggesting a deep, underlying stasis, or intensely contrasting and abrupt, depicting lattice shards that fracture and collide at rapid intervals.

statement: This sketch presents a microscopic view of a beeswax lattice undergoing rapid mechanical stress and fracture. The geometric shards—represented as ellipses with varying sizes and orientations—move at high velocities across the canvas, building up stress until sudden collisions cause them to shatter and reform. The color palette shifts between intense contrasting hues (orange-red) during moments of high stress, creating a visual metaphor for the mechanical forces at play. Connections between nearby shards pulse with this stress intensity, forming a dynamic network that continuously reforms as shards collide and scatter. The constant motion and abrupt transformations evoke the fragility and resilience of crystalline structures under pressure.
